extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in enumerative combinatorics and algebraic combinatorics
extracted.subtask_description: Techniques and solution-method guidelines for solving advanced exercises in enumerative combinatorics (generating functions, bijections, finite fields, matrices over F_q, and related algebraic methods). Aimed at producing or verifying combinatorial identities, counting formulas, and generating-function derivations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a substitution to transform sequences and derive recurrences
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting g(n) = 2^n f(n) (or similar multiplicative rescaling) to obtain a simpler recurrence for g(n) which may be easier to recognize or solve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example in text: setting g(n) = 2^n f(n) leads to a recurrence for g(n) whose solution is g(n) = E_{2n+1}. This technique is used to transform recurrences into recognisable sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guess generating function from initial values and verify algebraically
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute initial terms f(0), f(1), f(2), ... to conjecture a closed form or generating function, then verify the guess by checking the required functional equation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple examples: compute f(0)=1,f(1)=2,f(2)=6,... to guess a form (e.g., 1/2 or Catalan generating function) and then verify by substitution into identities like P = F(x^2) or other relations; 'To verify the guess, one must check...' is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use equation references / previously established identities
rubrics_metrics.description: Invoke earlier numbered equations (e.g., 'Use equation (1.98)') to derive results rather than re-deriving from scratch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text repeatedly instructs to 'Use equation (1.98)' or other prior equations to shortcut derivations—follow local references in the source when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relate finite differences to exponential generating functions via Taylor's theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply Taylor's theorem to convert finite difference expressions into evaluations of exponential generating functions: Δ^n f(k) related to e^{-x}F(x+t), etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: 'By Taylor’s theorem and (a) we have Δ^n f(k) ... = e^{-x}F(x+t).' Use this to transform difference-table problems into generating-function statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kernel method for solving functional equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the kernel method (introduce a kernel factor and solve for unknown generating functions by canceling the kernel) to obtain generating functions with two-variable kernels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text note: 'The solution to this exercise is a simple example of a technique known as the kernel method.' Use the kernel method especially for functional equations in two variables; see Knuth and Prodinger references for further examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Möbius inversion for multiplicative/logarithmic relations
rubrics_metrics.description: When log F(x) = sum_{n>=1} g_n x^n/n, use the Möbius inversion formula to express a_n in terms of g_d (and vice versa) via sums over divisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: derivation of a_n from g_n using n * g_n = sum_{d|n} d * a_d and then Möbius inversion an = (1/n) sum_{d|n} d g_d μ(n/d). Use this for arithmetic / multiplicative generating-function manipulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use cyclotomic polynomial evaluations at 1 and roots of unity for combinatorial sums
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze sums/products at roots of unity and use properties of cyclotomic polynomials Φ_n(1) (equals p if n is a prime power, otherwise 1) to extract coefficients or evaluate combinatorial quantities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text discusses evaluating expressions at q = ζ^r (roots of unity) and relates to Φ_n(1). Use these evaluations to determine surviving terms in root-of-unity sums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit parity / even-odd decomposition of power series
rubrics_metrics.description: When solving functional equations for power series, decompose logarithms or series into odd and even parts; an arbitrary even power series E(x) with E(0)=1 can appear in the general solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: solving for H(x) from H(x)H(-x)=G(x) leads to log H(x) = odd_part + arbitrary even series; 'E(x) := e^{E1(x)} is an arbitrary even power series with E(0)=1.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use trigonometric identities to invert arctan-type functional relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Manipulate arctan/tan identities (addition formulas, half-angle formulas) to express one power series f(x) in terms of another g(x), allowing an arbitrary even power series parameter when signs aren't fixed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: use tan(x+y) formula and half-angle identities to obtain f(x) from g(x) up to an arbitrary even series h(x) with h(-x)=h(x). Careful sign selection is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal group law / Hopf algebra approach for two-variable formal series
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and use the formal group law structure F(x,y) = f(f^{-1}(x)+f^{-1}(y)) and related formal series techniques when problems involve composition laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: 'The concept of a formal group law goes back to S. Bocher...' and gives examples such as f(x)=x, e^x-1, tan x, sin x; see Frölich and Lenart for Hopf-algebraic/combinatorial perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use composition/inversion constraints on power series coefficients
rubrics_metrics.description: For A(x)=x + a2 x^2 + ..., analyze conditions A(A^{-1}(x))=x or A(A(x))=x to deduce polynomial relationships among the coefficients (e.g., determination of odd/even coefficients).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text shows how equating coefficients in compositions gives polynomial relations p_{2n} in a2,...,a_{2n}, and thereby determines subsets of coefficients uniquely; use algebraic ideal arguments as shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translate functional relations into differential equations to solve for generating functions
rubrics_metrics.description: If B'(x)/B(x) = A'(x)/A(x) or similar, turn the relation into a differential equation and solve with given initial conditions to find B(x) (or other unknown series).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text suggests solving B'(x)/B(x)=A'(x)/A(x) for B(x) by integrating and using initial condition B(0)=a0; operator methods like (1+I+I^2+...)A may also be used formally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use bijections / adapted ordered bases to count linear transformations
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct canonical bijections (e.g., adapt an ordered basis to successive images Ai(V)) to count nilpotent or other classes of matrices by mapping them to tuples determined by images of basis vectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: adapt an ordered basis to the sequence V ⊃ V1 ⊃ ... ⊃ Vr=0, get a canonical ordered basis y, and associate A with the tuple (A(y1),...,A(yn-1)). This yields counts of nilpotent matrices. Several alternative counting proofs (induction, double-counting) are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Count polynomials or matrices via factorization into irreducibles and product-form generating functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Express generating functions as Euler-type products over degrees (1 - x^d)^{-β(d)} by accounting for monic irreducible factors or companion-matrix combinatorics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to count monic polynomials, discriminant-restricted polynomials, and to derive identities like those in Exercise 1.183; choose the appropriate product over degrees with multiplicities β(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use discriminant and Galois-group parity arguments to determine when discriminants are squares
rubrics_metrics.description: Relate whether the discriminant of a polynomial over F_q is a square to whether the Galois group (viewed as permutations of roots) is contained in the alternating group; for irreducible over F_q this reduces to parity of degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: 'the discriminant of an irreducible polynomial g(x) of degree n over a field K is a square in K iff the Galois group is contained in A_n' and for irreducibles over F_q generated by an n-cycle this implies square iff n is odd; use this to count square vs non-square discriminants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify adjoint orbits of Mat(n,F) via Jordan block data and Frobenius action
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent adjoint orbits by data (partition λ and multisets of eigenvalues) leading to a decomposition of orbits indexed by λ with affine parameter spaces of size q^{ℓ(λ)}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text gives three proofs culminating in Ω_q ∼= ⨆_{λ ⊢ n} F_q^{ℓ(λ)} and counts orbits by q^{ℓ(λ)}; useful when enumerating conjugacy classes in Mat(n,q).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply the Pentagonal Number Formula and q-series differentiation for asymptotics/modularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Pentagonal Number Formula and differentiations with respect to q to derive congruence or divisibility properties of q-analog sequences (e.g., ω*(n,q) divisibility by q^2 conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: deduce patterns like ω*(n,0) and behavior of ω*(n,q) by applying pentagonal identities and differentiating generating-product identities with respect to q.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use recurrence relations plus induction for orthogonal polynomial identities
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a three-term recurrence (e.g., (n+1)P_{n+1}(x) = (2n+1)xP_n(x) - nP_{n-1}(x)) and then use induction to prove identities/properties of the polynomial family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: 'One method of proof is to first establish the three term recurrence ... and then use induction.' Standard tactic for Legendre-like polynomials and related sequences.
